We need to determine number of methyl groups in the sample's molecule. We have no direct description of molecule. We can get NMR spectra to infer. Use proton NMR to see signals for CH3 (singlet, doublet, etc). Could also use carbon NMR to see CH3 carbon signals (around 10-30 ppm). Probably easiest: get proton NMR and count distinct methyl signals? But need number of methyl groups, not distinct types. Could count integration of methyl peaks. But integration not provided maybe.

We could get HSQC to map protons to carbons. But maybe simpler: get carbon NMR and count signals in methyl region (0-40 ppm). That gives number of unique methyl carbons, not total count if equivalent groups. Might need integration.

Better: get proton NMR and look for peaks around 0.9 ppm (triplet) etc. But need count of methyl groups total. Could be ambiguous.

Maybe the sample is known? No description. So we must actually run NMR tools. Use proton_nmr_spectra.
